agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

import subprocess, json, re, itertools, random

    a="".join(random.choice("abcd") for _ in range(la))
    b="".join(random.choice("abcd") for _ in range(lb))
    pairs.append((a,b))

    a="".join(random.choice("abc") for _ in range(la))+".txt"
    b="".join(random.choice("abc") for _ in range(lb))+".txt"
    pairs.append((a,b))

    ops=[{"source":f"/tmp/t1/{s}","target":f"/tmp/t1/{t}"} for s,t in batch]

]:
    print("ARGS",args)
    # pty spawn captures
    out=[]
    def read(fd):
        data=os.read(fd,1024); out.append(data); return data
    # pty.spawn returns exit? it echoes? Use script instead
    import pty as p

    master, slave=os.openpty()

    buf=b""
    while True:
        try:
            d=os.read(master,4096)
        except OSError: break
        if not d: break
        buf+=d
    proc.wait(); os.close(master)

    buf+=d

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ColorMode {
    Always,
    Never,
    Auto,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TransformKind {
    Upper,
    Lower,
    Ascii,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct CommonOptions {
    pub force: bool,
    pub backup: bool,
    pub silent: bool,
    pub color: ColorMode,
    pub dump: bool,
    pub dump_prefix: String,
    pub no_dump: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TraversalOptions {
    pub include_dirs: bool,
    pub recursive: bool,
    pub max_depth: Option<usize>,
    pub hidden: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RegexArgs {
    pub expression: String,
    pub replacement: String,
    pub paths: Vec<String>,
    pub common: CommonOptions,
    pub replace_limit: Option<usize>,
    pub replace_transform: Option<TransformKind>,
    pub traversal: TraversalOptions,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct FromFileArgs {
    pub dumpfile: String,
    pub common: CommonOptions,
    pub undo: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ToAsciiArgs {
    pub paths: Vec<String>,
    pub common: CommonOptions,
    pub traversal: TraversalOptions,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Commands {
    Regex(RegexArgs),
    FromFile(FromFileArgs),
    ToAscii(ToAsciiArgs),
}

fn common_args() -> Vec<Arg> {
    vec![
        Arg::new("dry_run")
            .short('n')
            .long("dry-run")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .conflicts_with("force")
            .help("Only show what would be done (default mode)"),
        Arg::new("force")
            .short('f')
            .long("force")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Make actual changes to files"),
        Arg::new("backup")
            .short('b')
            .long("backup")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Generate file backups before renaming"),
        Arg::new("silent")
            .short('s')
            .long("silent")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Do not print any information"),
        Arg::new("color")
            .long("color")
            .value_parser(["always", "never", "auto"])
            .default_value("auto")
            .help("Set color output mode"),
        Arg::new("dump")
            .long("dump")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .conflicts_with("no_dump")
            .help("Force dumping operations into a file even in dry-run mode"),
        Arg::new("dump_prefix")
            .long("dump-prefix")
            .value_name("DUMP_PREFIX")
            .default_value("rnr-")
            .help("Set the dump file prefix"),
        Arg::new("no_dump")
            .long("no-dump")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Do not dump operations into a file"),
    ]
}

fn traversal_args() -> Vec<Arg> {
    vec![
        Arg::new("include_dirs")
            .short('D')
            .long("include-dirs")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Rename matching directories"),
        Arg::new("recursive")
            .short('r')
            .long("recursive")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .help("Recursive mode"),
        Arg::new("max_depth")
            .short('d')
            .long("max-depth")
            .value_name("LEVEL")
            .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(usize))
            .requires("recursive")
            .help("Set max depth in recursive mode"),
        Arg::new("hidden")
            .short('x')
            .long("hidden")
            .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .requires("recursive")
            .help("Include hidden files and directories"),
    ]
}

pub fn build_cli() -> Command {
    let regex = Command::new("regex")
        .about("Rename files and directories using a regular expression")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("expression")
                .required(true)
                .help("Expression to match (can be a regex)"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("replacement")
                .required(true)
                .help("Expression replacement (use single quotes for capture groups)"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("paths")
                .value_name("PATH(S)")
                .required(true)
                .num_args(1..)
                .help("Target paths"),
        )
        .args(common_args())
        .arg(
            Arg::new("replace_limit")
                .short('l')
                .long("replace-limit")
                .value_name("LIMIT")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(usize))
                .help("Limit of replacements, all matches if set to 0"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("replace_transform")
                .short('t')
                .long("replace-transform")
                .value_name("REPLACE_TRANSFORM")
                .value_parser(["upper", "lower", "ascii"])
                .help("Apply a transformation to replacements including captured groups"),
        )
        .args(traversal_args());

    let from_file = Command::new("from-file")
        .about("Read operations from a dump file")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("dumpfile")
                .value_name("DUMPFILE")
                .required(true)
                .help(""),
        )
        .args(common_args())
        .arg(
            Arg::new("undo")
                .short('u')
                .long("undo")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Undo the operations from the dump file"),
        );

    let to_ascii = Command::new("to-ascii")
        .about("Replace file name UTF-8 chars with ASCII chars representation")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("paths")
                .value_name("PATH(S)")
                .required(true)
                .num_args(1..)
                .help("Target paths"),
        )
        .args(common_args())
        .args(traversal_args());

    Command::new("rnr")
        .version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
        .about("RnR is a command-line tool to rename multiple files and directories that\nsupports regular expressions\n")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .subcommand_required(true)
        .subcommand(regex)
        .subcommand(from_file)
        .subcommand(to_ascii)
}

fn parse_common(matches: &clap::ArgMatches) -> CommonOptions {
    let color = match matches.get_one::<String>("color").map(|s| s.as_str()) {
        Some("always") => ColorMode::Always,
        Some("never") => ColorMode::Never,
        _ => ColorMode::Auto,
    };
    CommonOptions {
        force: matches.get_flag("force"),
        backup: matches.get_flag("backup"),
        silent: matches.get_flag("silent"),
        color,
        dump: matches.get_flag("dump"),
        dump_prefix: matches
            .get_one::<String>("dump_prefix")
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "rnr-".to_string()),
        no_dump: matches.get_flag("no_dump"),
    }
}

fn parse_traversal(matches: &clap::ArgMatches) -> TraversalOptions {
    TraversalOptions {
        include_dirs: matches.get_flag("include_dirs"),
        recursive: matches.get_flag("recursive"),
        max_depth: matches.get_one::<usize>("max_depth").copied(),
        hidden: matches.get_flag("hidden"),
    }
}

fn parse_paths(matches: &clap::ArgMatches) -> Vec<String> {
    matches
        .get_many::<String>("paths")
        .map(|values| values.cloned().collect())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

pub fn parse() -> Commands {
    let matches = build_cli().get_matches();
    match matches.subcommand() {
        Some(("regex", sub)) => {
            let transform = match sub
                .get_one::<String>("replace_transform")
                .map(|s| s.as_str())
            {
                Some("upper") => Some(TransformKind::Upper),
                Some("lower") => Some(TransformKind::Lower),
                Some("ascii") => Some(TransformKind::Ascii),
                _ => None,
            };
            Commands::Regex(RegexArgs {
                expression: sub.get_one::<String>("expression").unwrap().clone(),
                replacement: sub.get_one::<String>("replacement").unwrap().clone(),
                paths: parse_paths(sub),
                common: parse_common(sub),
                replace_limit: sub.get_one::<usize>("replace_limit").copied(),
                replace_transform: transform,
                traversal: parse_traversal(sub),
            })
        }
        Some(("from-file", sub)) => Commands::FromFile(FromFileArgs {
            dumpfile: sub.get_one::<String>("dumpfile").unwrap().clone(),
            common: parse_common(sub),
            undo: sub.get_flag("undo"),
        }),
        Some(("to-ascii", sub)) => Commands::ToAscii(ToAsciiArgs {
            paths: parse_paths(sub),
            common: parse_common(sub),
            traversal: parse_traversal(sub),
        }),
        _ => unreachable!("a subcommand is required"),
    }
}

                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(usize))
                .help("Limit of replacements, all matches if set to 0"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("replace_transform")
                .short('t')
                .long("replace-transform")
                .value_name("REPLACE_TRANSFORM")
                .value_parser(["upper", "lower", "ascii"])
                .help("Apply a transformation to replacements including captured groups"),
        )
        .args(traversal_args());

    let from_file = Command::new("from-file")
        .about("Read operations from a dump file")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("dumpfile")
                .value_name("DUMPFILE")
                .required(true)
                .help(""),
        )
        .args(common_args())
        .arg(
            Arg::new("undo")
                .short('u')
                .long("undo")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Undo the operations from the dump file"),
        );

    let to_ascii = Command::new("to-ascii")
        .about("Replace file name UTF-8 chars with ASCII chars representation")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("paths")
                .value_name("PATH(S)")
                .required(true)
                .num_args(1..)
                .help("Target paths"),
        )
        .args(common_args())
        .args(traversal_args());

    Command::new("rnr")
        .version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
        .about("RnR is a command-line tool to rename multiple files and directories that\nsupports regular expressions\n")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .subcommand_required(true)
        .subcommand(regex)
        .subcommand(from_file)
        .subcommand(to_ascii)
}

fn parse_common(matches: &clap::ArgMatches) -> CommonOptions {
    let color = match matches.get_one::<String>("color").map(|s| s.as_str()) {
        Some("always") => ColorMode::Always,
        Some("never") => ColorMode::Never,
        _ => ColorMode::Auto,
    };
    CommonOptions {
        force: matches.get_flag("force"),
        backup: matches.get_flag("backup"),
        silent: matches.get_flag("silent"),
        color,
        dump: matches.get_flag("dump"),
        dump_prefix: matches
            .get_one::<String>("dump_prefix")
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "rnr-".to_string()),
        no_dump: matches.get_flag("no_dump"),
    }
}

fn parse_traversal(matches: &clap::ArgMatches) -> TraversalOptions {
    TraversalOptions {
        include_dirs: matches.get_flag("include_dirs"),
        recursive: matches.get_flag("recursive"),
        max_depth: matches.get_one::<usize>("max_depth").copied(),
        hidden: matches.get_flag("hidden"),
    }
}

fn parse_paths(matches: &clap::ArgMatches) -> Vec<String> {
    matches
        .get_many::<String>("paths")
        .map(|values| values.cloned().collect())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

pub fn parse() -> Commands {
    let matches = build_cli().get_matches();
    match matches.subcommand() {
        Some(("regex", sub)) => {
            let transform = match sub
                .get_one::<String>("replace_transform")
                .map(|s| s.as_str())
            {
                Some("upper") => Some(TransformKind::Upper),
                Some("lower") => Some(TransformKind::Lower),
                Some("ascii") => Some(TransformKind::Ascii),
                _ => None,
            };
            Commands::Regex(RegexArgs {
                expression: sub.get_one::<String>("expression").unwrap().clone(),
                replacement: sub.get_one::<String>("replacement").unwrap().clone(),
                paths: parse_paths(sub),
                common: parse_common(sub),
                replace_limit: sub.get_one::<usize>("replace_limit").copied(),
                replace_transform: transform,
                traversal: parse_traversal(sub),
            })
        }
        Some(("from-file", sub)) => Commands::FromFile(FromFileArgs {
            dumpfile: sub.get_one::<String>("dumpfile").unwrap().clone(),
            common: parse_common(sub),
            undo: sub.get_flag("undo"),
        }),
        Some(("to-ascii", sub)) => Commands::ToAscii(ToAsciiArgs {
            paths: parse_paths(sub),
            common: parse_common(sub),
            traversal: parse_traversal(sub),
        }),
        _ => unreachable!("a subcommand is required"),
    }
}

import subprocess, os, shutil, json, re, sys, glob

def snapshot():
    snap=[]
    for root,dirs,files in os.walk(BASE):
        dirs.sort()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            p=os.path.join(root,d); rel=os.path.relpath(p,BASE)
            if os.path.islink(p): snap.append(("linkdir",rel,os.readlink(p)))
            else: snap.append(("dir",rel))
        for f in sorted(files):
            p=os.path.join(root,f); rel=os.path.relpath(p,BASE)
            if os.path.islink(p): snap.append(("link",rel,os.readlink(p)))
            else:
                try: snap.append(("file",rel,open(p,'rb').read()))
                except Exception as e: snap.append(("fileerr",rel,str(e)))
    # work dir dump files
    work=[]
    if os.path.exists(WORK):
        for f in sorted(os.listdir(WORK)):
            p=os.path.join(WORK,f)
            if os.path.isfile(p):
                content=open(p,'rb').read()
                # normalize timestamps in filename and content
                name=re.sub(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}_\d{6}', 'TS', f)
                content=re.sub(rb'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}', b'TS', content)
                work.append((name,content))
            else: work.append((f,"<dir>"))
    return snap,work

def setup(spec):
    shutil.rmtree(BASE, ignore_errors=True); shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True)
    if os.path.islink(BASE) or os.path.isfile(BASE): os.remove(BASE)
    os.makedirs(BASE, exist_ok=True); os.makedirs(WORK, exist_ok=True)
    for item in spec:
        kind=item[0]
        if kind=="file":
            p=os.path.join(BASE,item[1]); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True); open(p,'w').write(item[2] if len(item)>2 else "content-"+item[1])
        elif kind=="dir":
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(BASE,item[1]), exist_ok=True)
        elif kind=="link":
            p=os.path.join(BASE,item[1]); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True); os.symlink(item[2],p)
        elif kind=="dump":
            # item[1] operations list with {BASE} placeholder
            ops=[]
            for s,t in item[1]: ops.append({"source":s.replace("{B}",BASE),"target":t.replace("{B}",BASE)})
            open(DUMP,'w').write(json.dumps({"date":"2020-01-01 00:00:00","operations":ops}))
        elif kind=="workfile":
            open(os.path.join(WORK,item[1]),'w').write(item[2] if len(item)>2 else "")

def run_one(exe,args):
    # replace {B} in args
    args=[a.replace("{B}",BASE).replace("{W}",WORK).replace("{D}",DUMP) for a in args]
    r=subprocess.run([exe]+args, cwd=WORK, capture_output=True, text=True)
    snap=snapshot()
    return (r.stdout,r.stderr,r.returncode,snap)

/// Both paths are expected to have a parent and a file name; the
/// values are unwrapped directly, mirroring the behaviour for
/// operations built from ordinary file paths.
///
pub fn format_operation(operation: &Operation) -> String {
    let op = operation;
    let source_parent_path = op.source.parent().unwrap().to_str().unwrap();
    let source_filename = op.source.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap();
    let target_parent_path = op.target.parent().unwrap().to_str().unwrap();
    let target_filename = op.target.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap();
    let source = if source_parent_path.is_empty() {
        grey(source_filename)
    } else {
        format!(
            "{}{}",
            grey(&format!("{}/", source_parent_path)),
            grey(source_filename)
        )
    };
    let target_parent_part = if target_parent_path.is_empty() {
        String::new()
    } else {
        green(&format!("{}/", target_parent_path))
    };
    format!(
        "{} -> {}{}",
        source,
        target_parent_part,
        colored_diff(source_filename, target_filename)
    )
}

use crate::deunicode::deunicode;
use crate::error::Error;
use regex::{Captures, Regex};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ReplaceTransform {
    Upper,
    Lower,
    Ascii,
}

pub trait Solver {
    fn solve(&self, file_name: &str) -> String;
}

pub struct RegexSolver {
    expression: Regex,
    replacement: String,
    limit: usize,
    transform: Option<ReplaceTransform>,
}

impl RegexSolver {
    pub fn new(
        expression: &str,
        replacement: &str,
        limit: usize,
        transform: Option<ReplaceTransform>,
    ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        let expression = Regex::new(expression).map_err(Error::BadExpression)?;
        Ok(RegexSolver {
            expression,
            replacement: replacement.to_string(),
            limit,
            transform,
        })
    }

    fn apply_transform(&self, text: String) -> String {
        match self.transform {
            Some(ReplaceTransform::Upper) => text.to_uppercase(),
            Some(ReplaceTransform::Lower) => text.to_lowercase(),
            Some(ReplaceTransform::Ascii) => deunicode(&text),
            None => text,
        }
    }
}

impl Solver for RegexSolver {
    fn solve(&self, file_name: &str) -> String {
        let replacement = self.replacement.clone();
        let result = self.expression.replacen(file_name, self.limit, |caps: &Captures<'_>| {
            let mut expanded = String::new();
            caps.expand(&replacement, &mut expanded);
            expanded
        });
        // The transformation applies to the expanded replacement of each
        // match. `replacen` with a closure already expands captures, so a
        // second pass is used when a transformation is requested to make
        // sure captured text is transformed too.
